description:
FOUND s461ar (agent AR, round 18) by a probe taken while measuring #911, and
PRE-EXISTING on both emission paths.  Not caused by anything in that session.

perl's capture variables are DYNAMICALLY SCOPED to the enclosing BLOCK: a
match inside a sub or a bare block sets $1 there, and leaving the scope
RESTORES the outer value.  PCL's captures are plain globals, so the inner
match's value leaks out.  Probed 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl at 4d2c17e:

    'abcdef' =~ /(bcd)/;
    sub f { 'xyz' =~ /(y)/; return "in=$1" }
    my $r = f();
    print "$r out=$1\n";                  perl: in=y out=bcd    PCL: in=y out=y
    { 'pqr' =~ /(q)/; print "block-in=$1\n"; }
    print "block-out=$1\n";               perl: bcd             PCL: q

The AGREEING half is worth recording so nobody re-derives it: a successful
match with NO capture groups DOES clear $1 in both (`'xyz' =~ /y/` then $1 is
undef), and a FAILED match leaves it alone in both.  The divergence is purely
the scope restore.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ITS OWN ROWS: it silently corrupts any test that calls a
reporting helper between a match and a read of $1 -- which is why
Pl/t/caret-vars-01.t's #873 helper carries a comment forbidding s/// inside it,
and why the #911 table there re-establishes its match at the TOP of the helper
rather than at the call site.  A future guard that does not know this will
write a row that passes for the wrong reason.

SHAPE OF A FIX (unmeasured, and the cost is the point): perl saves the capture
state on the scope stack.  PCL would have to bind the capture state around
every BLOCK that can contain a match -- every sub body, every bare block --
which is a per-scope save/restore on the hottest path there is.  Measure a
cheap version first: only save when the scope actually CONTAINS a match
(a compile-time fact the emitter already computes for other purposes), and
only the groups the pattern has.

BAR: the two probes above; op/pat and re/ companion legs (they are full of
match-in-helper shapes); the counting-loop bench rows unmoved.

=== NEW CONSUMER (s531c, 2026-11-01): core Text::Wrap, so every Pod::Simple::Text paragraph ===
#4103 dissolved into this task: Text::Wrap::wrap() reads `$remainder = $2` right after `$r .= unexpand(...)`, and Text::Tabs::unexpand's own matches leak out, so wrap("  ","  ","abc\n") loses its last newline (perl "  abc\n", PCL "  abc").  Pod-Simple t/fcodes_s.t rows 13-34 (22 board rows) now cite this task.  Any core / CPAN module that calls a helper between a match and its capture read hits it silently.  Probes: scratch/s531c/p/cap1.pl (five spellings: sub call, s/// inside the callee, inside an if block, under /gc, bare block), scratch/s531c/p/WrapCopy.pm + wrap2.pl / wrap3.pl (the Text::Wrap chain, with $unexpand = 0 as the control) in the s531c worktree.

=== s543t (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-28): THE SUB HALF IS DONE, found again as #2560 ===
Math::BigRat->new("49/4") was 1 because BigRat::new calls Math::BigFloat->new($1) and then ->new($2), and BigFloat::new's own matches overwrote the caller's $2.  Fixed in cl/: p-sub-frame (every named and anonymous sub) wraps its body in %p-match-scope -- *p-match-saved* is bound to :unsaved per frame, %p-match-record (the one writer of the match state) snapshots the state it is about to overwrite at the frame's FIRST successful match (%p-match-snapshot: :none for an empty state, else one vector), and the frame's NORMAL exit restores it (%p-match-restore), after the return value is copied (`return $1` is the callee's).  A sub that matches nothing allocates nothing; cost: one special binding + one compare per call, a snapshot + restore per call of a sub that matches (the s543t bench rows sub-call / sub-match).  Guard Pl/t/match-vars-01.t row 52 (the task's two probes' sub half + Text::Wrap's helper shape), inverse-verified on cababb9d.
STILL OPEN here: (a) a DIE that unwinds through the frame does not restore (like p-loc-save, the normal exit only) -- `if ("st" =~ /(s)(t)/) { eval { dies() }; print $1 }` with dies() matching: perl s, PCL the callee's; (b) the BLOCK half is #684 (bare block, loop body, map/grep/sort blocks, eval BLOCK / STRING are not scopes); (c) perl restores WHICH OP is current, PCL the STATE -- a recursive call through the same op differs (#5543, rare); (d) an `$_[0]` aliasing `$2` reads the CURRENT match in perl after the callee matched (perl `y|` undef, PCL keeps the value) -- rare, not filed.
subject: capture variables are not dynamically scoped: perl RESTORES $1 on block/sub exit, PCL does not
triage_reason: capture variables are not dynamically scoped (one family with #684)
